title: Streaming schema-deviation reconciliation and idempotent tool-call fallback policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: When Redwood streams partially structured objects (JSON fragments, interleaved tool-call envelopes, or incremental records) to customers or downstream tool gateways, schema deviations can appear mid-stream due to model tokenization, truncation, or conditional branching. We need a deterministic reconciliation layer that detects schema deviation early, surfaces a clear, machine-readable error envelope, attempts automated recovery when safe, and ensures tool invocations remain idempotent and observable. This ticket defines the acceptance criteria, test cases, rollout plan, and guardrails for the feature.
acceptance_criteria: Stream-level schema header: every streaming response must emit a top-level 'x-schema-version' header in the first chunk; consumers may include 'schema-accept' to indicate supported versions.

Deviation detection: if subsequent chunks would produce an object that violates the advertised schema (missing required field, unexpected type, structural truncation), the runtime emits a 'schema_deviation' envelope with a stable error code and optional recovery hint before the stream closes.

Partial-object recovery: for deviations that are patchable (e.g., trailing field missing due to truncation), the runtime must attempt a bounded auto-repair up to one re-emit attempt using model/variant fallback; this must be controlled by a per-call header 'reconciliation=auto|manual|off'.

Idempotent tool calls: every tool invocation emitted from the model must include an idempotency token (idempotency_token) and a deterministic call-signature (tool_name + normalized args) such that retries or replays can be detected and suppressed by downstream gateways.

Safe fallback: if auto-repair fails or is disabled, the stream should close with a 'partial_schema_error' envelope including: error_code, human_message, suggested_next_action (retry_with_backoff | request_full_payload | call_tool_direct), and a stable reconcile_token for correlation in subsequent calls.

Streaming error boundary: consumers must be able to resume from a reconcile_token via a separate non-streaming 'reconcile' endpoint; acceptance requires the reconcile endpoint to accept the token and return either: a full canonical object, a delta patch, or an explicit refusal with reason.

Observability: every schema_deviation, auto-repair attempt, tool-call, and reconcile request must emit structured spans and metrics (tagged with model, schema_version, route, customer_id) and appear in the Console under a new 'streamed-structured-errors' dashboard.

Backpressure & flow-control: when a downstream tool signals that it cannot accept calls (503 or backpressure flag), the platform must buffer up to the configured buffer_limit (default 2MB) and then: (a) pause the stream with a 'backpressure' envelope if buffer exceeded, or (b) trigger fallback policy (call via alternate gateway or enqueue for later).
Security & privacy: reconcile_token must be short-lived (TTL <= 5 minutes) and opaque; tokens must be logged only as hashes in audit logs and never include PII in plaintext.

Compatibility: the runtime must support existing non-streaming structured-output consumers unchanged; streaming schema header and envelopes are optional for older clients but toggled via 'stream_schema' feature-flag per customer.
success_tests: Unit test: synthesize stream where last chunk truncates required field 'address.postal_code' -> expect 'schema_deviation' envelope, one auto-repair attempt, and then canonical object returned when successful.

Integration test: simulate tool gateway returning intermittent 503 during tool-call in stream -> expect idempotency token on every call, buffered payloads up to 2MB, then 'backpressure' envelope when exceeded and metric 'streaming.backpressure.triggered' increments.
E2E test: consumer requests reconcile with reconcile_token -> reconcile endpoint returns full canonical object; verify token TTL enforcement and audit log hashing of token.
Property test: generate randomized partial JSON fragments; verify that deviation detection always emits a single schema_deviation per call and never duplicates reconcile_tokens.

Load test: run 1k concurrent streams with mixed auto-repair enabled/disabled; verify 99th percentile added latency for streaming responses stays within SLO (< 120ms per-chunk processing overhead) and CPU/GPU overhead < 10% baseline.
Security review test: token entropy check, replay attack simulation where attacker replays reconcile_token after TTL -> expect denial and audit entry.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary - 10% customers): enable feature-flag 'stream_schema_v2' for internal and a small customer cohort. Monitor 'streamed-structured-errors' dashboard and error budget. Phase 2 (gradual - 30/60/100): expand canary groups, enable auto-repair default for new customers. Phase 3 (policy defaults): set reconciliation=manual for high-security customers, add console toggle. Rollback criteria: >3x baseline rate of schema_deviation or >5% of reconcile requests returning 'refused' within 24h, or consumer-facing incidents reported in top-tier customer SLAs.
